references.text: John the Baptist sends his disciples to Jesus to ask if He is the one who was to come, which shows John's significant role and recognition.
Herod hears about Jesus' miracles and believes that John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, which shows Herod's fear and respect for John.
Herod wants to kill John, but fears the crowd because they regard him as a prophet, which underscores John's high status and Herod's fear.
Herod imprisons John for rebuking him concerning Herodias, but it is also mentioned that Herod feared John, which parallels his fear and respect shown in Mark 6:20.
